title: LlamaToaster GPU offload speed and memory study: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on RX 6600 XT (Vulkan)

report.name: The Spill Tax
report.note: Private artifact. This file is the underlying data; the report is the narrative.

model.nglMaxNote: 40 transformer layers + 1 output pseudo-layer, llama.cpp's -ngl ceiling for this model

harness.note: Measurement choreography is the application's own, unmodified (worker/src/runtimeBench.ts executeCurvePoint, spawnRuntimeServer). Orchestration around it was ad hoc scripts outside production code, since deleted.

environment.backgroundGpuUsage: Normal desktop session (compositor, browser, LibreHardwareMonitor) ran throughout; whole-adapter readings include it, roughly 1.1-1.5 GiB above per-process.

method.perLoad: Every load is a fresh llama-server process at one (ngl, ctx). Previous process fully exits (SIGTERM, 5s grace, then SIGKILL; awaited) before the next starts. No delay between loads.
requestChoreography: warm_discard: 32 prompt tokens, n_predict 8, cache_prompt false. Not counted.
cold_timed: promptTokens = max(64, ctx - 128), n_predict 1, cache_prompt false, streamed. Source of PP and TTFT.
warm_repeat x3: same prompt, n_predict 64, cache_prompt true, streamed. Source of TG (mean of the 3).
method.prompt: Pre-tokenized mixed-register filler text (worker/src/fillerPrompt.ts), not repetitive tokens.
method.telemetry: GPU memory polled once per second for the whole life of each load (spawn to teardown) via worker/src/vram.ts readGpuMemory: Windows GPU Process Memory for per-process dedicated/shared, adapter-wide counters for global. Means and maxima therefore include the model-loading ramp.
method.spill: llama.cpp's own device buffer report parsed from startup stderr (model + KV + compute buffers on the GPU; host buffers excluded), minus the peak per-process dedicated VRAM observed after the model finished loading (shared/gpuSpill.ts measureGpuSpill). Positive = bytes served from system RAM instead of VRAM. Small negative values are clean loads (reading noise).
method.listDevices: Sweep D only: `llama-server --list-devices` executed immediately before each load; parsed '(<total> MiB, <free> MiB free)'.
method.percentileRule: Aggregates use nearest-rank: sort values, take index ceil(p/100 * n) - 1. With n = 3, p90 and p99 both equal the maximum; p50 is the middle value. With n = 1 all are the single value.
method.timeouts: Sweeps C and D wrapped completion requests in a 15-minute AbortSignal (the production path has no request timeout). llama-server startup readiness budget is the app's own 120 s.

sweeps.description: Speed sweep of ngl 3,4,5,6,7,8,14 x ctx 1k/2k/8k/16k. The full 28-point ladder walked three times as three separate script invocations (pass = invocation), so repeats of a point are never adjacent in time. Captures PP/TTFT/TG, spill, claimed, post-load dedicated peak, and global VRAM/shared percentiles over the load. No per-process means.
Memory-telemetry sweep over the same 28 points, single pass. Captures claimed plus per-process and global VRAM/shared as mean and max over the load. No speed metrics.
High-offload sweep of ngl 17,20,23,26,29,32,35,38,41 x 4 contexts, single pass, speed and memory together. Skip rule: once a context fails at some ngl, larger contexts at that ngl are not attempted.
Summit sweep of ngl 16 and 18 x 4 contexts, 3 runs each, interleaved (run 1 of 16, run 1 of 18, run 2 of 16, ...). Speed, memory, and --list-devices free before each load.

loads.pass: Pass (sweep A) or run (sweep D) number, 1-based. Always 1 for single-pass sweeps.
loads.promptTokens: Tokens sent in the cold_timed and warm_repeat prompts.
loads.error: Failure message when status is failed.
loads.ppTps: Prompt processing, tokens/s = timings.prompt_n / timings.prompt_ms from llama-server on the cold_timed request.
loads.ttftMs: Client-observed time to first streamed chunk on cold_timed. See caveats: plateaus near 30 s.
loads.e2eColdMs: Full wall-clock duration of the cold_timed request. Use this, not ttftMs, as prefill duration.
loads.tgTps: Token generation, tokens/s, mean of the 3 warm_repeat samples; each = tokens_predicted / (e2e - ttft).
loads.tgStddevTps: Sample stddev (n-1) of the 3 warm_repeat rates. Null where not recorded.
loads.tgSampleCount: Warm repeat samples in tgTps. Null where not recorded.
loads.spillCause: layers | cache | null, as classified by probeSucceeded. Mostly null in these sweeps (atSmallestContext was not set).
loads.claimedMib: llama.cpp's self-reported GPU device buffer total, MiB. Static per load.
loads.dedicatedLoadedPeakMib: Peak per-process dedicated VRAM after load (spill's subtrahend). Sweep A only.
loads.procVramMeanMib: Per-process dedicated VRAM, mean over the load.
loads.procVramMaxMib: Per-process dedicated VRAM, max over the load.
loads.procSharedMeanMib: Per-process shared (system-RAM-backed) GPU memory, mean over the load.
loads.procSharedMaxMib: Per-process shared GPU memory, max over the load.
loads.globalVramMeanMib: Whole-adapter dedicated VRAM used, mean over the load (all processes).
loads.globalVramMaxMib: Whole-adapter dedicated VRAM used, max over the load.
loads.globalSharedMeanMib: Whole-adapter shared GPU memory, mean over the load.
loads.globalSharedMaxMib: Whole-adapter shared GPU memory, max over the load.
loads.globalVramPercentilesMib: Sweep A only: {min,p25,p50,p75,p90,p95,p99,max,n} of whole-adapter VRAM samples over the load. min includes pre-load samples.
loads.globalSharedPercentilesMib: Sweep A only: same, for whole-adapter shared memory.
loads.listDevicesFreeMib: Sweep D only: free MiB reported by llama-server --list-devices just before the load.
loads.listDevicesTotalMib: Sweep D only: total MiB reported by --list-devices.
loads.wallMs: Wall time of the whole load: spawn, load, requests, teardown.
loads.ttftPlateauSuspect: Derived: true when ttftMs is 29-31 s but e2eColdMs exceeds it by > 1.5 s (keep-alive artifact); null when either is missing.

fields.points: Per-(ngl, ctx) aggregates exactly as displayed in the report. For ngl 3-14, speed and spill come from sweep A (n=3) while the memory means/maxima come from sweep B (single pass). For 16/18, everything comes from sweep D (medians of per-run means, max of per-run maxima). For 17 and 20-41, sweep C (n=1). 'Max' fields for speed are the highest of n; for memory they are the maximum sample.

caveats: TTFT is not first-token latency for long prefills: 50 of 70 measured points report ~30 s regardless of actual prefill duration (34-866 s), consistent with a periodic SSE keep-alive. PP is unaffected (server-side prompt_ms). Use e2eColdMs for prefill duration.

Every warm_repeat in every sweep was flagged cache_evicted by the harness (prefix cache never held). TG is computed from the post-first-token window and matches the app's independent probe path, so it is treated as valid.
ngl 17 and 20-41 are single measurements (n=1). In particular whether ngl 16 or 17 is the true decode peak is unresolved.
First loads of a session place memory differently: ngl 14 pass 1 spilled less than passes 2-3; ngl 16 and 18 run 1 spilled more than runs 2-3. Later runs are near-identical to each other.
ngl 41 at ctx 8k did not become ready within 120 s; ngl 41 at 16k was therefore not attempted.
GPU clock and temperature were not captured (LibreHardwareMonitor web server not running). Thermal effects cannot be excluded from this data.
Memory means include the model-loading ramp, so procVramMeanMib sits somewhat below the steady-state level for short loads.
Single machine, single model, single driver/build. No claims generalise beyond it without replication.
findingsAsOfReportV8: Prefill is binary: ngl 3-6 run 100-147 tok/s, ngl 7-41 run 19-40 tok/s, with no intermediate values. The split does not track spill size: ngl 5 spills ~158 MiB and is fast, ngl 8 spills ~141 MiB and is slow.
Past the cliff, spill grows 27x (366 MiB at ngl 7 to 10,012 MiB at ngl 41) with no further prefill cost.
Decode peaks on a plateau at ngl 16-17 (~13 tok/s at ctx 1k) and falls to 8.47 tok/s at full offload, which is the slowest decode setting tested.
Per-process dedicated VRAM saturates at ~6.1-6.8 GB from about ngl 17 up; claimed memory beyond that goes to shared ~1:1. Held + shared exceeds claimed by a near-constant ~500 MiB.

llama-server --list-devices reported 7,378 MiB free before every recorded load, yet held VRAM never exceeded 6,833 MiB and spill begins at a claim of ~2,408 MiB. It is not a usable fit predictor on this system.
excludedRuns: Earlier exploratory runs in the same investigation (a first 12-point single pass of ngl 14/7/6, an 8-point ngl 5/4 addition, back-to-back spill-repeat and probe-ladder delay experiments) were superseded by the restart that produced sweep A and are not reflected in the report, so they are excluded here.

integrity.note: points[].ppP50Tps, tgP50Tps and spillP50Mib for every n=3 configuration were recomputed from loads[] with the stated percentile rule and matched the report.
